drafts.title: $7.7 billion. What people 60 and over lost to scams last year, and AI is making the calls sound real (pack AP6, AI for normal people, 55+)
drafts.window: Wed 1-3 PM MT. Don't post the same day as the Verizon bill payoff.
drafts.angle: One big number and one rule a family can set up tonight: a safe question only the real person would know. Medicare Open Enrollment is the season scammers love. Monday's Grok Bot credit-card quote is the bots-working-for-you side; this is the defense side.
bullets: FBI IC3 2025 Elder Fraud Report: 201,266 complaints from people 60 and over, $7.748 billion lost, up 59% from 2024. Average loss about $38,500.
Senate Aging Committee (via FEDweek, Oct 19): AI voice cloning powers the grandparent scam, and scam kits sell for as little as $20.

The Independent (Oct 16): identity expert Aaron Painter's grandmother nearly fell for a cloned-voice call of him. She caught it because the caller used a nickname the family never used. His advice: verify the person, don't try to spot the fake.
Medicare Open Enrollment runs Oct 15 to Dec 7. Medicare cards are free, and Medicare won't call out of the blue asking for your number.
Hang up and call back on a number you already have. Report at reportfraud.ftc.gov or ic3.gov.
drafts.body:
SHORT VERSION:
$7.7 billion. That's what people 60 and over lost to scams last year, per the FBI.

AI can copy a grandkid's voice now.

Our family [has / is setting up] a safe question only the real person would know.

Does your family have one yet?

LONGER VERSION:
$7.7 billion. That's what people 60 and over lost to scams last year, according to the FBI. Up 59 percent in one year.

Here's the part that gets me. AI can copy a grandkid's voice now, and the scam kits sell for about $20.

One grandmother caught a fake call of her own grandson because the voice used a nickname the family never uses. That's the whole trick. Don't try to spot the fake. Check the person.

So our family [has / just set up] a safe question. Something only the real person would know. Not a birthday, not the dog's name that's all over Facebook. [what kind of question we picked, not the real one.]

If the voice on the phone can't answer it, hang up and call back on the number you already have.

And since it's Medicare open enrollment until Dec 7: if somebody calls about your "new Medicare card," hang up. The card is free, and Medicare isn't calling you out of the blue for your number.

AI isn't the bad guy here. It's a tool, and the crooks picked it up first. A ten second family rule beats it.

Does your family have a safe question yet?

drafts.target: AARP's fraud account or a big verified senior-finance account posting about Open Enrollment: reply with the safe-question line.

drafts.title: $38 a month. What Colorado Springs solar owners will pay more under new rules (pack AP5, solar, Colorado, who pays)
drafts.window: Thu ~7 PM MT (best cell on a weak day), or Wed 1-3 PM if #3 moves.
drafts.angle: A Colorado solar story with a hard dollar number, recirculating this week. His take as a solar owner on the other side of the state: ask what happens if your utility changes the rules before you sign. Battery mention one line max or none. Not the rooftop-solar growth stat (LIVE Sun) and not backup power (Powerwall quote LIVE Mon).
bullets: Colorado Springs Utilities (city-owned): City Council approved new net metering rules Sept 22, 2026 (Gazette). Recirculating Oct 19.
Solar customers pick one: a new $1.00 a day grid access charge with time-of-day rates (on-peak 5-9 PM weekdays), or a demand charge on their highest 15-minute on-peak use.
CSU's own estimate: either option raises a typical solar bill about $38 a month (2027 rates).
Agreements before April 1, 2027 are grandfathered until April 1, 2032. New customers move sooner.
CSU says solar customers were shifting about $400 a year each onto non-solar neighbors; solar owners say it guts their payback (CPR: one owner invested $40,000).
drafts.body:
SHORT VERSION:
$38 a month. That's how much more Colorado Springs Utilities says solar owners will pay under its new rules, including a $1 a day grid charge.

I'm a solar owner on the other side of the state. [my take: ___]

If you're shopping for solar, would this change your mind?

LONGER VERSION:
$38 a month. That's how much more Colorado Springs Utilities figures a typical solar owner will pay under its new rules.

Solar customers there get two choices. A $1 a day grid charge plus rates that cost more from 5 to 9 PM on weekdays. Or a charge based on their single heaviest 15 minutes of use in those evening hours.

If you signed up before April 1, 2027, you're grandfathered until 2032. Everybody after that gets it sooner.

The utility says solar homes were pushing about $400 a year each onto neighbors without panels. Solar owners say it wrecks the payback they were sold. One guy put $40,000 into his system.

I've got solar on the other side of the state with [Xcel / Grand Valley Power]. [my take: fair or not? While we were on the road our panels made ___ kWh.]

Here's the one thing I'd tell anybody shopping for solar. Ask the installer what happens if your utility changes the rules. Your contract doesn't lock in the utility's rates. Colorado Springs says that right on its own page.

Would this change your mind about buying solar?
